comments.author: Priya Sharma
comments.body: Load test with 500 doomed deliveries: 500 terminal events, no extras. Deployed to production.

content.text: Load test with 500 doomed deliveries: 500 terminal events, no extras. Deployed to production.

When webhook delivery exhausts its retry budget, the worker parks the message on the DLQ and stops. Subscribers never receive a terminal failure event, so their ops dashboards stay green while deliveries are dead.

After the 8th attempt (or the 24-hour retry ceiling), the delivery pipeline should emit webhook.delivery_failed to the subscription's endpoint with the last status code, attempt count, and nextAction=manual_retry. Instead the DLQ write is silent aside from an internal metric.
Hypothesis: the failure publisher is only invoked from the synchronous reject path, not from the DLQ admission hook. The async retry chain marks the job terminal without calling emitTerminalFailure.
Customers monitoring only their own endpoint miss that Nimbus has given up, and support has no customer-visible trail when asked why events stopped.
